description: Go mosaic crazy with artist Amira Rogers! From beginners to experts, students will create their own small glass mosaic that they will be able to take home at the end of class. You will be able to choose what type of image you like to create, some ideas are house number, kitchen sign, fruit, anything you want, you choose! You will leave the class with your piece already finished. This class will be split into a step by step session where I will show you demonstrations of how to create mosaics from initial drawings to tools we use to cut and paste the glass itself, but you will spend the majority of the time working on your piece. Clean-up time is included in the duration of class, and usually the last 20 minutes of class are dedicated to cleaning your workstation. Mosaic work involves a mix of seated and standing activities. Handling glass and tools may require a certain level of dexterity. **Eligibility:** No previous experience required. Open to ages 12 and up. title: Just in Time
description: See some of the most extraordinary items from the New York Public Library's collections of the last 125+ years. Encounter manuscripts, artworks, letters, still and moving images. Solve puzzles, perform experiments, and explore scientific principles behind Native innovations and technologies in an interactive, family-friendly space. Explore Jim Henson’s work and learn about his transformative impact on popular culture. Experience a charming carousel that honors European and American traditions. Learn the remarkable story of the rescue of the Danish Jews during the Holocaust and the community's efforts during that time. Create with sound in MoMA's interactive space for families. Enjoy views of New York in a mobile tea room. Interact with site-specific sculptures throughout the city. Take photos with the Charging Bull, a symbol of optimism. Experience vibrant music and Latin dance inspired by Cuban culture. Explore timely art exhibits and discover the mysteries of nocturnal animals. View unique sculptures that fuse Indigenous world views with contemporary art. Invent and test toy vehicles in a hands-on lab. Celebrate the life of Bobby Darin with cabaret-style performances.

title: Planting Fields Spring 5K
description: Join us for the 5th Annual Spring 5K Walk/Run at Planting Fields Arboretum State Historic Park! Lace up your running shoes for a scenic journey through the breathtaking landscapes designed by the renowned Olmsted Brothers. As you run, jog, or walk the course, you’ll traverse a variety of terrains while immersing yourself in the beauty and history of the arboretum. Along the way, you’ll pass iconic landmarks including the Carshalton Gates and the picturesque Taxus Field, all surrounded by the vibrant colors of spring in bloom. Whether you’re a seasoned runner aiming for a personal best or simply looking to enjoy a refreshing morning outdoors with friends and family, the Spring 5K offers something for everyone. Open to participants of all ages and abilities, this event is designed to be both welcoming and inspiring. This year’s event also supports an exciting new chapter at Planting Fields the upcoming garden designed by world-renowned landscape designer Piet Oudolf, scheduled to open in fall 2026. Proceeds from the race help support the continued development and programming of this extraordinary garden, bringing a new horticultural destination to Long Island. All registrants will receive a personalized race bib and a commemorative finisher medal to celebrate their achievement. Celebrate the season of renewal on this iconic, verdant, and dynamic course. Don’t miss your chance to be part of this beloved community tradition—register today to secure your spot! For more information, please contact Lilly McGurk, Stewardship Director, at lmcgurk@plantingfields.org.

description: A one-day cycling fundraiser in Downtown Oyster Bay for riders of all ages and abilities supporting cancer research on Long Island. description: The Cheryl Diamond NYC 5K Cancer Schlep brings together hundreds of participants from the county, ranging in age from 5 – 90 years old, bound together in solidarity to raise the hopes of those battling breast and ovarian cancer. title: Tiny Toes & The Jazz Crew: A Musical Playground for the Whole Family
description: What happens when 'The Wheels on the Bus' hops on board with the legendary sounds of Duke Ellington, Thelonious Monk, and Miles Davis? East End Jazz is proud to announce the launch of 'Tiny Toes & The Jazz Crew,' a groundbreaking, interactive concert series designed to bridge the gap between early childhood playtime and the professional performing arts. This multi-generational experience invites families to step into a world where nursery rhymes blend seamlessly with jazz standards, proving that great music knows no age limit. 'We wanted to create a space where the next generation doesn’t just listen to music, but feels it,' says Iris Ornig, Director of East End Jazz. 'By pairing familiar melodies with sophisticated jazz arrangements, we’re inviting families to participate in the rhythm, movement, and spontaneous joy that defines this art form.' This isn’t your average performance. The series transforms playtime into a high-level artistic exchange, allowing children to experience jazz through the lens of play. Led by a 'Jazz Crew' of professional musicians from Long Island and NYC, the ensemble serves as both performers and mentors, guiding the audience through a journey of syncopation, scat-singing and instrumental discovery. Co-sponsored with the Bridgehampton Museum and East End Jazz.

title: Long Island Fleece & Fiber Festival
description: Hallockville Museum Farm will host its annual Long Island Fleece & Fiber Festival inviting visitors to experience the full journey of fiber — from raw fleece to finished textile — at its historic North Fork campus. A longtime spring tradition, the festival brings the cycle of fiber to life through live sheep and llama shearing with Long Island Yarn and Farm, spinning, and weaving demonstrations, along with a marketplace featuring more than two dozen regional fiber artists and artisans. A major highlight this year is the appearance of nationally recognized knitting expert Patty Lyons, who will lead two special sessions focused on practical techniques and problem-solving for knitters. Additional hands-on workshops include an introduction to weaving with the Paumanok Weavers, where participants can create their own scarf; a flat needle-felted farm landscape workshop led by Shamma Murphy; and basket weaving with Barbara Blossey-Chuvalas using natural materials such as silk, seagrass, and wool. Advance registration is required for workshops. In addition to demonstrations and workshops, visitors can explore a variety of family-friendly activities, including a children’s craft area, agricultural displays, and opportunities to meet the farm’s animals. Attendees are welcome to bring their fiber arts projects to work amongst like-minded creators. The festival also features live music by the Old Time Jam, local food vendors, and a bake sale hosted by Hallockville Bakers.

Along the way, you’ll pass iconic landmarks including the Carshalton Gates and the picturesque Taxus Field, all surrounded by the vibrant colors of spring in bloom. Whether you’re a seasoned runner aiming for a personal best or simply looking to enjoy a refreshing morning outdoors with friends and family, the Spring 5K offers something for everyone. Proceeds from the race help support the continued development and programming of this extraordinary garden, bringing a new horticultural destination to Long Island. Class is limited to 16 students between the ages of 11-15. Participants should bring their own snacks & drinks.

title: Courage to Act: Rescue in Denmark
description: Learn the remarkable story of the rescue of the Danish Jews during the Holocaust. Together, Jewish and non-Jewish neighbors of all ages mobilized to create one of the most effective—and exceptional—examples of mass resistance and escape in modern history. State-of-the-art technology and creative storytelling immerse visitors in this inspiring story. Age-appropriate themes of separation, bravery, and resilience help young people make connections to their own lives and reflect on the dangers of prejudice—as well as their own potential for compassionate, moral, and courageous collective action and upstanding. Asso visit the Garden of Stones, a landscape artwork and living memorial garden of trees growing from stone was planted by the renowned artist Andy Goldsworthy., Holocaust survivors, and their families in 2003.

title: Living History: Let’s Celebrate Pinkster and Pinkster Stroll
description: This Pinkster Stroll will feature a group of Black New Yorkers dressed in historically inspired garb walking from Dyckman Farmhouse Museum to the New York Historical in commemoration of enslaved and free Black people in 17th- and 18th-century Dutch New York who celebrated Pinkster, the oldest African American holiday. Join us at New-York Historical Society to welcome them into the building at the end of their long walk, and to discover how the Christian feast of Pentecost celebrated by the Dutch evolved into a Black American festival used by Black New Yorkers to gather with family and friends, and reconnect with their African cultures. This program is a partnership between the New York Historical, Dyckman Farmhouse Museum, and Not Your Momma’s History.

title: Hablemos: GRAFFITI
description: In the mid-20th century, the urban landscape of New York City changed dramatically with the advent of graffiti. Artists used the city as their canvas. Their artistic surfaces varied from walls of abandoned buildings to subway cars. Initially, graffiti art was criminalized and people who participated in the activity were at risk of being arrested, but over time street art became accepted and even celebrated. In this session of Hablemos, see examples of tags (signatures) and graffiti that are part of the collection of The New York Historical. To complete the program draw your own tag using the different styles of letters and a rainbow of colors inspired by artists like Blade, Lady Pink, Keith Haring and more. Advanced registration required.

title: Move NYC: Annual Parkour + Movement Festival
description: The Movement Creative returns to New Design High School’s athletic field with their parkour and movement festival and fundraising benefit, MOVE NYC. On May 22-24, the nomadic parkour company along with dozens of volunteers will build a massive parkour park on the athletic field at 28 Essex Street, and fill it with parkour athletes, climbers, martial artists, and acrobats. Everyone is invited to join the movement community to train, learn, teach, and move together to help raise money for New Design’s physical education program. Sunday 5/24 will feature several dedicated workshops for youth as well as Danish Field Games, Capture The Flag, and Ultimate Dodge Ball. With raffle drawings, snacks and beverages, a massage tent, face painting, and athletic gear for sale in the heart of the bustling Lower East Side, MOVE NYC is the perfect destination for families in town for the Memorial Day Weekend!

Marking a decade of impact in Southeast Queens, this beloved annual event brings together music and dance traditions from around the world alongside hands-on arts activities designed for children of all ages. title: Richard Shindell in NYC
description: Join us for an unforgettable evening with singer-songwriter Richard Shindell at the beautiful Church of Saint Mary the Virgin in Times Sq. Richard Shindell lives as both an immigrant and emigrant, crossing thresholds, that informs his illumination of the human experience through narrative song. Shindell has inhabited a Zen Buddhist monastery and busked in the streets of Paris. Originally from New York, now living in Buenos Aires, Argentina, Shindell is a writer whose songs paint pictures, tell stories, juxtapose ideas and images, inhabit characters, vividly evoking entire worlds along the way and expanding our sense of just what it is a song may be. Meticulously recorded over three years in New York and Buenos Aires, his most recent release, Careless, offered an ambitious, luxurious, full-length statement. Shindell immersed himself in the studio, allowing the time and latitude to explore, experiment, take risks—to play—as each of these eleven songs was given form and substance. While his signature acoustic guitar style is used to good effect, Careless also found Shindell plugging in more. “The wider sonic and dynamic range of the electric has been a real inspiration. Rejuvenating.” During the pandemic, Shindell stayed in Argentina, out on the wide open Pampa, reading, writing, taking walks, doing a little experimental recording, and tending the garden. He now returns to the road for a limited number of performances. Innovative, original and occasionally spiritual, Shindell’s songs weave tales that interchangeably champion the downtrodden, exalt the disaffected or wax empathetic to those lost to society’s fringes. From lighthearted ballads and adulterous love songs, to dirges and diatribes that skillfully skewer politics, prejudice, war and religion, to the comic point-of-view of a cow stuck in a barbed wire fence, he has a unique ability to morph into the soul of the many and varied personalities he casts as narrators in certain songs—veritable novellas framed in haunting acoustic melodies.

title: Riopy
description: Jean-Philippe Rio-Py, known to the world as RIOPY, is a pianist and multi-instrumentalist composer with over a billion streams, sold-out concerts across continents, collaborations with the likes of Lana Del Rey, and a catalogue of albums that have topped the classical charts. But beneath the numbers lies something far more human: a story of resilience, survival, and a man who has discovered sound as a vessel for healing. 2026 marks the release of RIOPY’s fifth album Be Love-an appeal born out of the artist’s awe-inspiring journey of rediscovery and defiance, and a refusal to let fear or illness silence him. “It’s called Be Love because that’s the only thing that matters. Be love. And if we all love, then everything is fine,” he says simply. Be Love will see RIOPY sing for the very first time on a release. The composer-instrumentalist has utilized numerous ways to produce sound, just never his own voice. “I had this compulsion, this need to use my voice, because I think it’s one of the biggest fears I’ve had through my life. But it’s something I really enjoy doing.” He shares, “I started just whispering... it’s not a new me, it’s just an expansion of what I do. It felt right, because I needed to do this.

description: In this class we will be going over how to create work with a simple bubble and “blob”, whether it is abstract or literal. Beginners will learn the fundamentals of hot glass blowing/sculpting, while being able to create a final piece of their own that is their own work. Working with a bubble is fundamental for glass blowing and adding parts as the “blob” to create a piece as a whole. Students will work together and learn to manipulate molten glass (2000 degrees). Safety, color application, and tools will all be covered in a fun and exciting environment. The hot shop is a loud studio, and can get quite warm. Glassblowing involves a variety of activities including sitting, standing, and working with hot glass. The environment can be very hot and loud at times. Handling glass and tools may require a certain level of dexterity and ability to lift 5-10 lbs approximately. Eligibility: No previous experience required. Open to ages 14 and up. The glass needs to cool down overnight, so the students will have to return to UrbanGlass once notified to pick up their work. We recommend registering for classes early to reserve your spot!

title: OPEN LAB | ...Almost Right Away: Moving Company with Erica Enriquez
description: 2026 AiR Erica Enriquez presents a movement and language based workshop that invites audience participants to play with cardboard. What structures can be built, destroyed, flattened, filled, emptied or imagined by group motion? How can language be a generative mechanism for arriving at a movement beyond its initial meaning or purpose? How might material and language work in tandem with one another, guided by the subconscious connections drawn by audience participants? Using the song _The First Snow In Kokomo_ by Aretha Franklin as a portal, the workshop will be accompanied by the band **Ube Boys**, performing a set of improvisational music inspired by the lyrics 'Applegate discovered a coronet, almost right away.' Participants will be supplied with a room full of cardboard boxes, packing tape and dollies, while collectively considering the expansive potential of the words 'Almost', 'Right', and 'Away'.

title: Family Day at Perelman Performing Arts Center
description: Perelman Performing Arts Center NYC brings together families and artists for a day-long takeover of its indoor and outdoor spaces. Enjoy workshops, performances, interactive creation stations, dance battles, live music, and more. Activities and Performers include: AirLoom Beats: The art of beat boxing with Brooklyn Hip Hop educator Arabelle Luke. Ants on a Log: An interactive family concert full of humor and harmony, joy and justice. Baba Israel: Hip-hop theater artist and poet. Broken Box Mimes: Mime for a contemporary audience - unplugging creativity with joyful, movement-based storytelling. Bubble America: Performers specializing in bubble fun. Elena Moon Park and Friends: A joyous celebration of folk and children’s songs. look in look out: A temporary environment of play, perception, and collective attention through a large-scale parachute installation and participatory activation by artists Laurie Berg and Amy Rose Khoshbin, commissioned by PAC NYC. Mazma, Music & Magic From India & Beyond: World magician Shreeyash teams up with sitarist and overtone singer Neel Murgai for an intimate performance of magic, wonder, ragas, and rhythms. Music With A Message: 25-member youth group delivers powerful messages through creative renditions of songs and innovative original compositions. Natural Impressions: An all-ages workshop explores printmaking and tactile design using citrus stamps and seed-filled clay, encouraging creativity, sensory play, and connection to natural materials through pattern-making with teaching artist Paloma Nicholas. Parade: Artist Greg Corbino invites all ages to join a herd of giant elephant puppets made from recycled paper to reimagine the famous crossing of 21 elephants over the Brooklyn Bridge in May 1884—transforming the story into one that celebrates possibility and creativity in uncertain times. Commissioned by PAC NYC. Street Soccer: Free style soccer clinic and soccer trick performance with Spinny Vinny. Stompopolis!: An interactive installation where a reactive floor turns into sound by artist Tei Blow, commissioned by PAC NYC. Story Circles with The People’s Theatre: An interactive story circle with guest readers. Todo Migra!: Afro-Andean Funk transforms ancient Andean and Afro-Peruvian traditions into a live ritual of funk, resistance, and dance—in three languages.

title: Just in Time: Bobby Darin
description: See some of the most extraordinary items from the 56 million in the New York Public Library's collections of the last 125+ years. Encounter manuscripts, artworks, letters, still and moving images. Solve puzzles, perform experiments, play state-of-the-art computer simulations and find out how corn is like a dog in this interactive, family-friendly space. Explore scientific principles behind Native innovations and technologies. Explore Jim Henson’s groundbreaking work for film and television and his transformative impact on popular culture. This small, charming carousel, specially created to complement Bryant Park’s French classical style, is an homage to both European and American carousel traditions with French cabaret music. Learn the remarkable story of the rescue of the Danish Jews during the Holocaust. Together, Jewish and non-Jewish neighbors of all ages mobilized to create one of the most effective—and inspiring—rescue efforts in history. Create with sound in MoMA's latest interactive space for families. Listen, explore, play, and move. Drop in and choose from a variety of activities for all ages, from toddlers to teens. See the sights of New York in a double-decker bus transformed into a mobile tea room with a glass roof offering a wide field of view, and a bright, floral decor. Admire feminist pop-artist Ashley Longshore's brightly colored irreverent art throughout the cheerful two-story art gallery and shop. Carol Bove’s first museum survey fills the entire rotunda with assemblages of paperback books, intimate paper collages and towering steel sculptures. Interact with four new site-specific sculptures by The Art Students League of New York artists: Jason McCormack and Montana Simone in Riverside Park South at 61st Street, and Kenneth Doherty and Aseel Sawalha in Riverside Park North. Take photos with the 11-feet-tall, 7,000 pound bronze Charging Bull, a symbol of financial optimism and prosperity. Vibrant music by an onstage band and exuberant Latin dance are the draw in this celebration of Cuban culture. Explore timely art exhibits in a waterfront park with stunning Manhattan views. Discover the mysteries, adaptations, and surprises of animals that thrive in darkness. Learn about specialized senses that help animals survive in the dark. Four 10-feet tall sculptures reflect acclaimed artist Jeffrey Gibson's distinctive visual language. Invent, test, and perfect toy vehicles in a hands-on lab. Celebrate the dramatic life of Bobby Darin, writer of hits like 'Mack the Knife,' 'Beyond the Sea,' 'Splish Splash,' and 'Dream Lover' in intimate, cabaret-style staging.

title: Socrates Sculpture Park Exhibition
description: See some of the most extraordinary items from the 56 million in the New York Public Library's collections of the last 125+ years. Encounter manuscripts, artworks, letters, still and moving images. Solve puzzles, perform experiments, play state-of-the-art computer simulations and find out how corn is like a dog in this interactive, family-friendly space. Explore scientific principles behind Native innovations and technologies. Explore Jim Henson’s groundbreaking work for film and television and his transformative impact on popular culture. This small, charming carousel, specially created to complement Bryant Park’s French classical style, is an homage to both European and American carousel traditions with French cabaret music. Learn the remarkable story of the rescue of the Danish Jews during the Holocaust. Together, Jewish and non-Jewish neighbors of all ages mobilized to create one of the most effective—and inspiring—rescue operations in history. Create with sound in MoMA's latest interactive space for families. Listen, explore, play, and move. Drop in and choose from a variety of activities for all ages, from toddlers to teens. See the sights of New York in a double-decker bus transformed into a mobile tea room with a glass roof offering a wide field of view. Admire feminist pop-artist Ashley Longshore's brightly colored irreverent art throughout the cheerful two-story art gallery and shop. Carol Bove’s first museum survey fills the entire rotunda with assemblages of paperback books, intimate paper collages, and towering steel sculptures. title: Reading Under Fire: Arming Minds & Hearts During Wartime
description: Poster House, the first museum in the United States dedicated to the global history of posters, will present four new exhibitions for the spring 2026 season. The two main exhibitions, Reading Under Fire: Arming Minds & Hearts During Wartime and From Monarchy to Modernity: Travel, Identity, & the Czechoslovak First Republic (1918–1938), will open to the public on April 23, 2026 and close on November 1, 2026. Reading Under Fire examines how books and the act of reading itself were mobilized to sustain morale among soldiers during World Wars I and II. As foot soldiers were required to carry all of their possessions, compact and portable forms of entertainment became essential. title: Charging Bull Photo Opportunity
description: See some of the most extraordinary items from the 56 million in the New York Public Library's collections of the last 125+ years. Encounter manuscripts, artworks, letters, still and moving. Solve puzzles, perform experiments, play state-of-the-art computer simulations and find out how corn is like a dog in this interactive, family-friendly space. Explore scientific principles behind Native innovations and technologies. Explore Jim Henson’s groundbreaking work for film and television and his transformative impact on popular culture and learn how Henson and his team of builders, performers, and writers brought to life beloved characters. This small, charming carousel, specially created to complement Bryant Park’s French classical style, is an homage to both European and American carousel traditions with French cabaret music. Learn the remarkable story of the rescue of the Danish Jews during the Holocaust. Together, Jewish and non-Jewish neighbors of all ages mobilized to create one of the most effective—and inspiring—efforts to save lives. Create with sound in MoMA's latest interactive space for families. Listen, explore, play, and move. Drop in and choose from a variety of activities for all ages, from toddlers to teens. See the sights of New York in a double-decker bus transformed into a mobile tea room with a glass roof offering a wide field of view. Admire feminist pop-artist Ashley Longshore's brightly colored irreverent art throughout the cheerful two-story art gallery and shop. Explore Carol Bove’s first museum survey that fills the entire rotunda with assemblages of paperback books, intimate paper collages and towering steel sculptures. Interact with site-specific sculptures by artists in Riverside Park South and Riverside Park North. Choose from 57 horses and two chariots on a charming carousel built in 1908. A fifteen-foot-tall bronze sculpture by artist and activist Molly Gochman honors caregiving in all its forms. Vibrant music by an onstage band and exuberant Latin dance are the draw in this celebration of Cuban culture. Brown bears, polar bears, and gorillas—a representation of endangered species—stand tall along Park Avenue Malls. Hop from one immersive space to the next in a spherical planet full of all kinds of bubbles, balloons and soap. Explore timely art exhibits in a waterfront park with stunning Manhattan views. Discover the mysteries of animals that thrive in darkness. Learn about specialized senses evolved to help animals survive in the dark.

title: Orienteering Meet at West Hills County Park – South
description: In an age where we rely on GPS navigation for every turn, could you still use a paper map? Are you ready to find out? Orienteering is a map reading skill that turns a walk in the woods into a, sometimes challenging, scavenger hunt. First, you orient the map, then orient yourself on the map, and try to find the “control flags” hidden in the woods and circled on the map. At each meet, there will be easy (all controls on trails about 3K), medium (controls visible from trails, 4-5K), and difficult courses (controls in the woods 5K+). Instruction is offered for beginners. Registration is from 10:30 am-1pm and competitors must finish by 3:30 pm.
